Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency - next steps

Hi Jordan - great to meet yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side:

- Recap: Acme wants region pinning for EU customers (data stored and processed in EU), US customers in US; cross-region failover needs to be controlled and approved.
- Open questions we promised to confirm:
  1) Which fields you classify as PII for this integration (full list).
  2) Desired retention windows for logs, requests, and backups (default vs. contractable).
  3) Acceptable behavior for cross-region failover and backups (encrypted at rest, key ownership constraints).
  4) Whether pseudonymization/tokenization of inputs is acceptable for EU-customer traffic.

Action items:
- Jordan to share your data classification doc and any minimum retention/backup constraints (SOC2/QS evidences).
- Redwood (Marissa + Aditya) to share a short architecture note showing how region pinning would look and options for failover/backups.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your security/infra lead (suggest Lina) and our infra lead (Marissa).

I attached a brief "redwood-region-pinning-overview.pdf" that shows the usual patterns we recommend (synchronous region pinning, same-region backups, and cross-region failover with contractual guardrails). If you can send your classification table and any contractual constraints, we'll turn around a proposed config and a narrow set of options for your security team to review.

Proposed times for the technical call: Wed 17 Mar 10:00-11:00 ET or Thu 18 Mar 14:00-15:00 ET. What works for you?

Thanks,

Hi Aditya - thanks for the clear recap. Attaching our data classification CSV (acme-data-classification.csv) - key points below:

- PII: includes full name, SSN, account number, debit/credit card PAN, date of birth, and direct contact details.
- Non-PII: aggregated analytics, model performance telemetry (we can share aggregated metrics).
- Retention: request that request-level logs (full request/response) are retained for 90 days by default; we will negotiate longer retention for fraud cases, but that's on a per-contract basis.
- Backups: backups must be stored in the same region as primary data. Cross-region backups require explicit contract language and must use customer KMS keys where possible.
- Cross-region failover: acceptable as long as the data in the recovery region is encrypted with customer-managed keys and we have documented controls and a tested failover runbook.

We can accept pseudonymization/tokenization for EU-customer data, provided the tokenization process is fully documented and keys are customer-managed.

Lina (cc) will take point on the technical call. We prefer Wed 17 Mar 10-11 ET.

-Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Director, Cloud Architecture | Acme Bank
jordan.hayes@acmebank.com | +1 212-555-0222

Subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency - next steps

Thanks Jordan - that's very helpful. A few clarifying questions so we can prepare the architecture doc for the call:

1) You mentioned "request-level logs (full request/response) retained 90 days" - is it acceptable for Redwood to store request metadata (timestamps, latencies, model variant ids) in a central (US) logging system while the request payloads and model inputs remain in-region (EU) for EU customers?
2) For backups: you said "same region" - do you require cold snapshots to never leave the region (even for encrypted transfers for DR testing), or is transfer allowed if encryption + customer KMS is used and we have a signed runbook?
3) Tokenization: pseudonymization is acceptable - can you share any minimum entropy/format requirements for tokens?

Next steps from our side: Marissa will prepare a short architecture diagram that shows two options: (A) strict same-region processing + synchronous failover with manual approval, (B) asynchronous cross-region failover with encrypted backups + customer KMS. I've attached a quick PNG we'll refine (region-pinning-architecture-diagram.png).

We'll bring Marissa (infra lead) and Vanessa (security ops) to the call to handle the KMS and logging controls discussion. Confirming Wed 17 Mar 10:00 ET for the technical deep-dive. I'll send a calendar invite with the agenda and a short read-ahead.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: region-pinning-architecture-diagram.png

Aditya/Marissa - confirmed, Wed 17 Mar 10:00-11:00 ET works for Lina and me. A couple quick notes ahead of the call:

- Logging: We can accept request metadata in a central (US) system for monitoring/alerting, but full request payloads must remain in-region for EU customers.
- Backups/DR: Cold snapshots must remain in-region; transient transfers for DR tests are allowed only with customer-managed KMS and signed change control.
- Tokenization: We are generally OK with pseudonymization. We will need to review tokenization design and key management.

Please add the HubSpot deal (ACME-2026-07) to the invite and include any SOC2 excerpts that show encryption-at-rest and key management controls (Marissa - can you attach a short SOC2 excerpt or the specific pages that call out KMS usage?).

Jordan
